title: A better Z′ can hide a worse measurement
summary: A higher Z′ can reflect nonlinear detector compression rather than a better assay. This article explains how bright-well variation can shrink while effect sizes become distorted, and how to check proportionality without confusing detector behavior with assay chemistry.

title: When does reading longer stop improving assay CV?
summary: Longer luminescence reads help when photon collection limits precision, but they cannot remove persistent differences between wells. This article shows how to compare repeated reads with independently prepared replicates, account for background noise, and choose a useful stopping point.

title: Read the plate map before you read the statistic
summary: Inspect spatial patterns alongside control statistics, then use those patterns to choose a follow-up check.

title: DNA quantification: five methods, five different answers
summary: DNA mass, target copies, amplifiable library molecules and fragment integrity are different measurements. Choose the answer your next experiment needs before choosing the instrument.

title: Microplate kinase assays: choose the event you need to measure
summary: ADP production, ATP depletion, substrate phosphorylation and target binding are useful measurements. They are not interchangeable evidence of kinase inhibition.

title: Automated confocal screening: compare the result, not the camera speed
summary: Six representative high-content imaging families compared by optics, simultaneous channels, live-cell conditions and the work required to turn a plate into reliable measurements.

title: HTRF: the ratio is not the whole result
summary: A stable HTRF ratio can conceal a major loss of signal, degraded precision, or a channel-specific interference. The article explains how to retain and interpret both emission channels, per-well ratios, and acquisition conditions.

title: ADP-Glo: the light comes after the kinase
summary: ADP-Glo light is the endpoint of a multistep detection sequence, so a lower signal can arise outside the kinase reaction. This article shows how to reconstruct the endpoint with ATP/ADP controls and interpret temperature, timing, conversion, and ATP-dependent potency.

title: CellTiter-Glo: when less light doesn’t mean fewer cells
summary: CellTiter-Glo measures ATP-dependent light, not cell number directly, so metabolism and detection conditions can change the signal independently of abundance. The article separates biological effects from reagent, temperature, mixing, and detector effects and proposes controls for each.

title: HiBiT: did the protein disappear, or just the light?
summary: A decrease in HiBiT light can reflect less tagged protein or a change in complementation, luciferase activity, lysis, background, or measurement. The article separates reporter abundance from accelerated degradation and outlines controls that test the detection system and native protein.

title: Your fluorescence polarization result is hiding two measurements
summary: A fluorescence-polarization value is calculated from parallel and perpendicular intensity measurements, and the ratio can hide low photon counts or timing mismatch. The article explains how to preserve both channels, interpret intensity and binding curves, and qualify tracer and reader behavior.

title: Your fluorescent label is part of the experiment
summary: Choose a fluorescence polarization tracer by matching lifetime to molecular motion, testing the conjugate and checking controls in the actual assay matrix.

title: One extra carbon can change the binding result
summary: A one-carbon linker change can alter tracer affinity and assay performance. Learn how to separate binding chemistry from your fluorescence polarization window.

title: Half the molecules and two thirds of the light
summary: Binding can change tracer brightness and shift an apparent Kd while the curve still fits beautifully. See the equations, controls and fluorescence data to keep.

title: Why is my luminescence signal lower on one plate reader than another?
summary: Learn why luminescence signals differ between readers and how to compare precision, linearity, temperature and crosstalk fairly.

title: What is the difference between analog and photon-counting luminescence detection?
summary: Compare analog and photon-counting readout, understand why longer integration cannot fix pulse overlap and qualify a useful linear range.

title: Can PMT saturation or signal compression occur without an overload warning?
summary: Learn how luminescence signal compression can precede an overload warning, distort results and appear in a practical detector-linearity check.

title: Why do my bright controls have excellent CVs while my weak samples are unreliable?
summary: Why bright controls can have excellent CV while weak samples remain unreliable, with photon statistics, background and working-range checks.

title: Why do I get negative fluorescence or luminescence values after blank subtraction?
summary: Understand negative fluorescence or luminescence after blank subtraction, diagnose blank mismatch and avoid bias from replacing negatives with zero.

title: Why does subtracting background make my CV worse?
summary: Learn why blank subtraction raises CV, how shared blanks create correlated uncertainty and why optical background prevention helps.

title: Why are repeated readings of one well precise while replicate wells disagree?
summary: Separate reader repeatability from dispensing, cell loading, position effects and preparation variability using a staged comparison.

title: How much does read height matter in fluorescence intensity?
summary: Optimize fluorescence read height using blanks and weak samples, with practical checks for plate geometry, fill volume and top versus bottom reads.

title: Why can increasing PMT gain make low-signal fluorescence CV worse?
summary: Why higher PMT gain can leave fluorescence precision unchanged or make it worse, with blank checks, gain tests and practical interpretation.

title: Should I use automatic gain on every plate in a screening run?
summary: When to keep plate reader gain fixed, when calibrated automatic range selection helps and how to check comparability across a screening run.

title: When does a wider fluorescence bandwidth improve sensitivity—and when does it make results worse?
summary: Learn when wider fluorescence bandwidth improves sensitivity, when it adds background and how to compare settings using weak samples and blanks.

title: Why do filter and monochromator readers perform differently at the same nominal wavelengths?
summary: Why matching wavelengths does not match plate reader performance, with bandwidth, blocking, dichroics and practical method-transfer checks.

title: What does a dichroic mirror change in a fluorescence measurement?
summary: How dichroic mirrors improve fluorescence light collection and excitation rejection, including monochromator optics and practical background checks.

title: Should I always read at a fluorophore's published excitation and emission peaks?
summary: Why published dye peaks are starting points, with FITC wavelengths, bandwidth overlap and practical tests using low positives and realistic blanks.

title: Top vs bottom read: which should I use for cell-based fluorescence?
summary: Choose top or bottom plate reading using cell location, medium background, plate transmission and matched controls while preserving assay biology.

title: NanoBRET: proximity needs a good alibi
summary: Improve NanoBRET assays with expression controls, simultaneous dual-emission detection, linearity checks and stable temperature. Includes worked examples.

title: TR-FRET: waiting doesn’t fix the wrong photons
summary: Troubleshoot HTRF and LanthaScreen assays by separating timing from spectral leakage. Learn when filters, excitation and reader controls improve results.

title: Why does an HTRF assay have good signal-to-background but poor Z-prime?
summary: Explain low HTRF Z-prime despite a good signal window using control variability, raw donor and acceptor data, and a worked example.

title: How should I optimize NanoBRET donor and acceptor filters?
summary: Choose assay-specific NanoBRET emission filters using raw channels, negative controls, ratio precision and simultaneous dual-emission detection.

title: Why does my HTRF assay still have high background after I increase the delay time?
summary: Troubleshoot persistent HTRF background with donor-only, acceptor-only and assay controls before changing delay, filters or integration time.

title: When does laser excitation improve an HTRF or TR-FRET assay?
summary: When laser excitation improves HTRF and TR-FRET precision or speed, with donor compatibility, paired detection and a practical comparison plan.

title: What does a dedicated TR-FRET detector add beyond time-gating a general-purpose PMT?
summary: Understand detector recovery, delayed background, spectral sensitivity and linearity when evaluating dedicated TR-FRET detection and laser excitation.

title: Why can a white plate outperform a black plate in a TR-FRET assay?
summary: Compare white and black TR-FRET plates through photon statistics, laser excitation, detector efficiency, crosstalk and assay-specific requirements.

title: Choosing assays for molecular glue and PROTAC screening
summary: Separate cellular engagement recruitment ubiquitination and protein loss

title: The ratio survived but the precision did not
summary: An unchanged FP ratio can hide lost precision. Follow photon-count examples and practical controls for attenuation, background and fluorescent compounds.

title: More receptor can make affinity harder to measure
summary: See how receptor concentration changes free ligand, shifts binding midpoints and limits Kd estimates, with worked examples and practical assay controls.

title: When does simultaneous dual-emission detection improve FP, TR-FRET or BRET precision?
summary: How simultaneous dual-emission detection reduces timing errors in FP, TR-FRET and BRET, and why weak channels and calibration still matter.

title: Are two PMTs enough for accurate ratiometric measurements, or do they need matching and calibration?
summary: Learn why simultaneous detection, relative channel calibration and linearity all matter for accurate FP, TR-FRET and BRET measurements.

title: Why can my NanoBRET ratio stay constant while the donor signal falls?
summary: Why a NanoBRET ratio can stay constant as donor light falls, how precision suffers and which raw signals and controls to inspect.

title: Why does the mP value of my free FP tracer change when I change its concentration?
summary: Diagnose concentration-dependent fluorescence polarization using raw channels, matched blanks, linearity checks and controls for tracer behavior.

title: Can I reuse the same FP G factor after changing filters, gain settings or readers?
summary: Know when to verify or recalibrate an FP G factor after changing filters, gains or readers, and why one matching reference value is insufficient.

title: Choosing a microplate: the plastic is part of the assay
summary: Choose microplates by surface, color, geometry and working volume. Use practical tests to separate useful signal from adsorption, crosstalk and evaporation.

title: Controls can look better when the detector stops telling the truth
summary: Tight controls can conceal signal compression. Qualify intermediate responses, optical linearity, crosstalk and temperature before accepting a screening window.

title: What causes crosstalk in 384- and 1536-well plates?
summary: Find the optical causes of microplate crosstalk, test bright-neighbor interference and distinguish leakage from sample carryover.

title: Why can crosstalk correction fix the mean but leave weak wells unreliable?
summary: See why subtracting crosstalk can correct a mean while leaving photon noise, and how to test optical suppression and correction independently.

title: What causes a plate edge effect: evaporation, temperature or cell biology?
summary: Diagnose microplate edge effects with volume, temperature and cell-distribution checks before applying corrections or changing the assay workflow.

title: Why does my assay have low Z-prime after moving from 384 to 1536 wells?
summary: Diagnose low Z-prime after miniaturizing from 384 to 1536 wells, including photon counts, cell loading, evaporation and read geometry.

title: Why does absorbance change when I change the volume, even at the same concentration?
summary: Understand why constant-concentration samples give different absorbance at different volumes, and when pathlength correction can help.

title: Can a plate lid or sealing film change my fluorescence, luminescence or absorbance results?
summary: Check transmission, fluorescence, condensation and read geometry before using a lid or sealing film during microplate measurements.

title: The plate is recording its temperature history
summary: Qualify liquid temperature during plate reads, busy runs and interruptions. Separate thermal drift from evaporation and optical crosstalk before correcting data.

title: The plate queue changed your IC50
summary: Map assay clocks, challenge plate queues and define restart rules. Use full curves, temperature control and reliable detection to test a screening workflow.

title: Your Alpha assay is also a thermometer
summary: Troubleshoot temperature effects in Alpha assays by testing liquid temperature, plate timing and control behavior under realistic screening conditions.

title: Why does my plate reader warm the plate when incubation is switched off?
summary: Understand plate-reader warming, room-temperature chamber control and practical temperature checks for CellTiter-Glo and Alpha assays.

title: Can a reader specified as “ambient +4°C” keep my assay at room temperature?
summary: Understand above-ambient temperature specifications, chamber heating and cooling, and the checks needed for stable room-temperature assay detection.

title: How can I tell whether the liquid in my plate has reached the reader's temperature setpoint?
summary: Distinguish chamber and liquid temperatures, understand thermal lag, and qualify equilibration across wells during a realistic plate-reader run.

title: Why do Alpha or glow-luminescence controls drift from the first plate to the last?
summary: Separate assay age, reagent changes and temperature drift when Alpha or glow-luminescence controls change from the first plate to the last.

title: Should I read a cell-based luminescence assay at 37°C or at room temperature?
summary: Choose detection temperature using CellTiter-Glo, RealTime-Glo MT and HiBiT Lytic protocols, with clear distinctions between live-cell and lytic assays.
